record.title: Šoltés graph uniqueness conjecture
record.statement: Let $C_{11}$ denote the cycle on eleven vertices. A **Šoltés graph** is a graph for which deleting any vertex leaves the Wiener index unchanged. **Šoltés graph uniqueness conjecture.** The cycle on eleven vertices, $C_{11}$, is the only Šoltés graph. The source notes that this is reinforced by the absence of Šoltés graphs among vertex-transitive graphs with fewer than $48$ vertices, but gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Nino Bašić, Martin Knor and Riste Škrekovski, “On regular graphs with Šoltés vertices”, arXiv:2303.11996 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11996

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

record.title: Ekin's missing crank inequality modulo 11
record.statement:
Let $p(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$, and let $M(r,11,n)$ denote the number of partitions of $n$ whose crank is congruent to $r$ modulo $11$. **Ekin's crank inequality.** For $n
geq 0$ with $n
eq 2$,

$$
M(1,11,11n+8)\geq \frac{p(11n+8)}{11}\geq M(0,11,11n+8).
$$

This is the remaining inequality in the family of crank inequalities modulo $11$ discussed after Ekin's results; the source presents it as a conjectural statement.
record.source_name: Nikolay Borozenets, “Deviation of the rank and crank modulo 11”, arXiv:2305.08751 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.08751

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of May 2023). “Some of the inequalities of Conjecture are proved in Corollary .”

record.title: Kostochka–Stocker equality conjecture for connected cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected cubic graph of order $n$, and let $\gamma(G)$ denote its domination number. The four graphs $G_{14.1}$, $G_{14.2}$, $G_{14.3}$, and the generalized Petersen graph $P(7,2)$ are the connected cubic graphs of order $14$ satisfying $\gamma(G)=5$.

**Kostochka–Stocker equality conjecture.** If

$$
\gamma(G)=\frac{5}{14}n,
$$

then

$$
G\in\{G_{14.1},G_{14.2},G_{14.3},P(7,2)\}.
$$

The claim extends the known classification at order $14$ to all connected cubic graphs; the source states that it is not known whether the $\frac{5}{14}$ bound is achievable for large order.
record.source_name: Csilla Bujtás andMichael A. Henning and Sandi Klavžar, “Partial domination in supercubic graphs”, arXiv:2305.19820 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.19820

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2023).

record.title: Conjecture on the supremum tail function for Rademacher sums on [√2,2]
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be the class of all Rademacher sums with variance $1$, and define

$$
F(x)=\sup_{X\in\mathcal{X}}\mathbb{P}(X>x),\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.
$$

**Conjecture for $F$ on $[\sqrt{2},2]$.** For $x\in[\sqrt{2},2]$,

$$
F(x)=\frac{1}{8}\quad\text{for }x\in[\sqrt{2},\sqrt{3}),
$$

$$
F(x)=\frac{1}{16}\quad\text{for }x\in[\sqrt{3},2),
$$

and

$$
F(2)=\frac{9}{256}.
$$

The conjecture extends the known result $F(x)=1/4$ for $x\in[1,\sqrt{2})$ to larger values of $x$. Determining $F(x)$ for large $x$ remains beyond current techniques, and the proposed values on this interval are stated as open in the source.
record.source_name: Lawrence Hollom and Julien Portier, “Tight lower bounds for anti-concentration of Rademacher sums and Tomaszewski's counterpart problem”, arXiv:2306.07811 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.07811

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

record.title: The amended Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ be positive integers, and let

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\max_{t\in\mathbb{R}}\min_{1\leq i\leq n}\lVert tv_i\rVert,
$$

where $\lVert x\rVert$ denotes the absolute distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. **The amended Loneliness Spectrum Conjecture.** One has either

$$
\exists s,k\in\mathbb{N},\quad k\leq n,\quad \operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)=\frac{s}{ns+k},
$$

or

$$
\operatorname{ML}(v_1,\ldots,v_n)\geq\frac{1}{n}.
$$

This modification is proposed after the original spectrum conjecture is disproved by examples such as $\operatorname{ML}(8,3,11,19)=7/30$ and $\operatorname{ML}(5,6,11,17,23,28)=8/51$. The paper reports experimental support and proves special cases, but does not establish the amended conjecture in general.
record.source_name: Ho Tin Fan and Alec Sun, “Amending the Lonely Runner Spectrum Conjecture”, arXiv:2306.10417 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.10417

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2023).

record.title: Reversed Dickson first-kind permutation polynomial classification
record.statement:
Let $p>3$ be a prime, and let $n$ satisfy $1leq nleq p^2-1$. Write $D_n(1,x)$ for the reversed Dickson polynomial of the first kind. A polynomial that permutes $\mathbb{F}_p$ is called a permutation polynomial (PP). **Reversed Dickson permutation conjecture.** $D_n(1,x)$ is a PP on $\mathbb{F}_p$ if and only if

$$
n = \begin{cases} 2,2p,3,3p,p+1,p+2,2p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 1 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p,p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 5 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p,p+2,2p+1 & \text{if } p\equiv 7 \pmod{12},\\ 2,2p,3,3p & \text{if } p\equiv 11 \pmod{12}.
\end{cases}
$$

The stated indices are known to be sufficient, while necessity remains open in general; the cases $p=5$ and $p=7$ are proved in the paper.
record.source_name: Jiaqi Fang, Neranga Fernando and Haoming Wu, “Reversed Dickson polynomials”, arXiv:2307.06325 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.06325

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2023).

record.title: The critical-region equation for randomized graph coloring experiments
record.statement:
Let $G(n,k,p)$ be a random graph with $n$ vertices, $k$ partitions, and edge probability $p$ between vertices from distinct partitions. The critical region is the range of parameters in which the algorithm performs poorly.

**Critical-region conjecture.** The critical regions are characterized by the equation

$$
\frac{2pn}{k} \approx \frac{16}{3}.
$$

This conjecture was proposed on the basis of experimental results and concerns the narrow parameter interval where the algorithm's performance deteriorates. The supplied text gives no evidence that it has been proved or refuted.
record.source_name: Boštjan Gabrovšek and Janez Žerovnik, “A fresh look to a randomized massively parallel graph coloring algorithm”, arXiv:2309.11961 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.11961

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2023).

record.title: The signed planar signature-packing conjecture
record.statement:
A signed graph is said to **pack** when its signature packing number attains the upper bound given by its negative girth. Let $\mathcal{C}_{10}$ and $\mathcal{C}_{11}$ be the classes of signed graphs described in the source; in particular, $\mathcal{C}_{10}$ is the class of signed bipartite graphs, while members of $\mathcal{C}_{11}$ can be switched to have all edges negative.

**Signed planar signature-packing conjecture.** Any signed planar graph in

$$
\mathcal{C}_{10}\cup\mathcal{C}_{11}
$$

packs.

This is listed as a conjecture equivalent or closely connected to the signed projective cube homomorphism conjecture. The general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Meirun Chen, Reza Naserasr and Alessandra Sarti, “Signed projective cubes, a homomorphism point of view”, arXiv:2406.10814 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10814

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2024).

record.title: Archer et al.'s Pell-number conjecture for cyclic pattern-avoiding permutations
record.statement:
Let $\pi$ be a cycle permutation in $S_n$, written in one-line notation as $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\cdots\pi_n$ and in cycle form as $\pi=(c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_n)$. A cycle permutation is in $\mathcal{A}^\circ_n(\sigma;\tau)$ when its one-line form avoids $\sigma$ and every cyclic rotation of its cycle form avoids $\tau$. **Archer et al.'s Pell-number conjecture.**

$$
\left|\mathcal{A}^\circ_n(2431;1324)\right|
$$

is the $(n-1)$st Pell number. Archer et al. proposed this enumeration for cyclic permutations avoiding $2431$ in one-line form and $1324$ in all cycle forms; the supplied status information leaves it open.
record.source_name: Junyao Pan, “On a conjecture about pattern avoidance of cycle permutations”, arXiv:2409.17482 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.17482

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2024). “Open Questions]) $\Big|\mathcal{A}^\circ_n(2431; 1324)\Big|$ is the $(n-1)^{\rm{st}}$ Pell number.”

record.title: Empirical recurrence conjecture for balanced 8 by 2n matrices
record.statement: Let $b_4(n)$ denote the number of balanced $8\times 2n$ matrices. A linear recurrence of order $9$ with polynomial coefficients of degree $36$ should be satisfied by the sequence $b_4(n)$; the recurrence is too large to print and is available at the cited website. This recurrence was obtained empirically by fitting sequence terms and is presented as conjectured, though the authors describe it as absolutely certain.
record.source_name: Robert Dougherty-Bliss, Christoph Koutschan, Natalya Ter-Saakov and Doron Zeilberger, “The (Symbolic and Numeric) Computational Challenges of Counting 0-1 Balanced Matrices”, arXiv:2410.07435 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07435

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: The cut-partition conjecture for t-triangles in fullerenes
record.statement:
Let $C_{56,622}$ and $C_{80,31924}$ denote the indicated fullerene graphs. A **cut-partition** of a hexagonal subgraph is the set of components generated by the stated cut-partition construction, and a **$t$-triangle** is the triangle type defined in the source. **Cut-partition t-triangle conjecture.** $C_{56,622}$ and $C_{80,31924}$ are the only fullerenes whose cut-partition consists solely of $t$-triangles.

The claim is based on numerical results about cut-partitions of hexagonal subgraphs. No proof or disproof is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Artur Bille, Victor Buchstaber and Evgeny Spodarev, “Some open mathematical problems on fullerenes”, arXiv:2410.19322 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.19322

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Further overcubic partition triple congruences
record.statement:
Let $\overline{bt}(n)$ denote the overcubic partition triple function, and let $n,\alpha\geq 0$. **The further overcubic partition triple congruence conjecture.**

$$
\overline{bt}(144n+42)\equiv 0 \pmod{384},
$$

$$
\overline{bt}\bigl(2^\alpha(72n+21)\bigr)\equiv 0 \pmod{128},
$$

$$
\overline{bt}\bigl(2^\alpha(72n+69)\bigr)\equiv 0 \pmod{128}.
$$

These conjectured congruences extend the two proved congruences modulo $128$ and $384$ stated immediately beforehand, and the supplied material gives no resolution beyond presenting them as conjectures.
record.source_name: Manjil P. Saikia and Abhishek Sarma, “Further Arithmetic Properties of Overcubic Partition Triples”, arXiv:2411.00013 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00013

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “We can go even further, but we leave the following as an open problem.”

record.title: No separation in Bayesian uniform-pricing approximation for quasi-regular buyers
record.statement:
Let asymmetric regular and quasi-regular buyers be compared using the revenue approximation of **Bayesian Optimal Uniform Pricing** to **Bayesian Optimal Mechanism**, with tight ratio denoted by $\calC_{{\sf BOM}}^{\textsf{Bayesian Optimal Uniform Pricing}}$. **Bayesian Optimal Uniform Pricing separation conjecture.** For asymmetric quasi-regular buyers, this tight ratio is the same as for asymmetric regular buyers, namely

$$
\calC_{{\sf BOM}}^{\textsf{Bayesian Optimal Uniform Pricing}}\approx0.3817.
$$

Thus the conjecture predicts no separation between regularity and quasi-regularity for this approximation problem; the stated regular-buyer bound is known, while the quasi-regular extension remains open.
record.source_name: Yiding Feng and Yaonan Jin, “Beyond Regularity: Simple versus Optimal Mechanisms, Revisited”, arXiv:2411.03583 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03583

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: Classification conjecture for 5-regular Ricci-flat graphs
record.statement: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a $5$-regular Ricci-flat graph. A graph is **of Cartesian product type** if it is the Cartesian product of a Ricci-flat $3$-regular graph and a Ricci-flat $2$-regular graph. **Classification conjecture.** If $G$ is a $5$-regular Ricci-flat graph, then $G$ is either isomorphic to $RF_{72}^{5}$ or is of Cartesian product type. The conjecture seeks a complete classification of $5$-regular Ricci-flat graphs; the existence of regular bone-idle graphs with odd vertex degree remains an open question.
record.source_name: Moritz Hehl, “Graphs with Lin-Lu-Yau curvature at least one and regular bone-idle graphs”, arXiv:2411.12772 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.12772

Status: **open** according to the source (as of November 2024). “The existence of regular bone-idle graphs with an odd vertex degree remains an open question.”

record.title: The alpha forest-cut conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\alpha$ satisfy

$$
2\leq \alpha\leq 3.
$$

A **forest cut** is a vertex cut whose induced subgraph is a forest.

**$\alpha$-FC conjecture.** If $G$ has no forest cut, then

$$
e(G)\geq \alpha(n-3)+3.
$$

This parameterized conjecture unifies lower bounds for connected graphs without forest cuts and is introduced to organize the structural arguments in the paper. The paper proves the case corresponding to its bound $\frac94n-\frac{15}{4}$, but does not establish the full parameterized assertion.
record.source_name: F. Botler, Y. S. Couto, C. G. Fernandes, E. F. de Figueiredo, R. Gómez, V. F. dos Santos and C. M. Sato, “Extremal Problems on Forest Cuts and Acyclic Neighborhoods in Sparse Graphs”, arXiv:2411.17885 (2025).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.17885

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

record.title: Neumann-Lara's dicoloring conjecture for oriented planar triangulations
record.statement: Let $G$ be an oriented planar triangulation, meaning a directed planar triangulation with no directed cycles of length $1$ or $2$. A vertex set is **acyclic** when it induces a subdigraph without directed cycles. **Neumann-Lara's dicoloring conjecture.** The vertices of $G$ can be partitioned into two acyclic sets. The conjecture is settled when directed triangles are absent and for oriented graphs on at most $26$ vertices, but remains widely open in general.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, François Dross, Kolja Knauer, Hoang La and Petru Valicov, “Partitions of planar (oriented) graphs into a connected acyclic and an independent set”, arXiv:2412.11774 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11774

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2024). “On the other hand, planarity is also essential, as shown by Horton who disproved a corresponding conjecture of Tutte .”

record.title: The dismantling characterization of trivial matroid homomorphism reconfiguration
record.statement:
Let $N$ be a matroid, and let $
\operatorname{Recol}_{\mathbb{M}}(N)$ denote the reconfiguration problem for matroid homomorphisms into $N$. A matroid **dismantles** to a retract $N'$ if a series of dismantling retractions has composition taking $N$ to $N'$, where a dismantling retraction is a retraction adjacent to the identity map. Write $M^\ell(K_1)$ for the loop on one vertex and $M(K_2)$ for the matroid of an edge.

**Dismantling characterization.** $\operatorname{Recol}_{\mathbb{M}}(N)$ is trivial if and only if $N$ dismantles to the loop $M^\ell(K_1)$ or the edge $M(K_2)$.

This would extend the corresponding characterization for graphs, where triviality of the reconfiguration problem is equivalent to dismantlability. The preceding results establish that dismantling to either of these two small matroids is sufficient; the converse is posed as an analogue for matroids and remains open.
record.source_name: Cheolwon Heo and Mark Siggers, “The complexity of matroid homomorphism reconfiguration”, arXiv:2503.19181 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.19181

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

record.title: Simonovits–Sós conjecture on P₄-intersecting families
record.statement:
Let $P_4$ denote the path on four vertices, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of labeled subgraphs of the complete graph $K_n$. The family $\mathcal{F}$ is **$P_4$-intersecting** if the edge intersection of any two members contains a copy of $P_4$.

**Simonovits–Sós conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}$ is a $P_4$-intersecting family of labeled subgraphs of $K_n$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}| \le 2^{\binom n2 - 3}.
$$

This conjecture asserted the sharpness of the trivial lower-bound construction. Christofides disproved it in 2012 by exhibiting a larger $P_4$-intersecting family.
record.source_name: Paul Hamrick and Gary Hu, “Lower Bounds on Intersection Families for Certain Graphs”, arXiv:2510.18064 (2025).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2023–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2310.18163](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18163).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.18064

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of October 2025). “In 2012, Christofides disproved this conjecture, using the graph shown in Figure .”

record.title: Lopez's path-transduction conjecture for non-2-well-quasi-ordered graph classes
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a hereditary class of finite graphs. **Lopez's path-transduction conjecture.** If $\mathcal{C}$ is not $2$-well-quasi-ordered, then $\mathcal{C}$ existentially transduces the class of all finite paths. This conjecture proposes a logical obstruction to $2$-well-quasi-ordering; it remains open in the general setting considered here.
record.source_name: Maël Dumas and Aliaume Lopez, “Well-quasi-ordered classes of bounded clique-width”, arXiv:2601.18571 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.18571

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2026). “AP Even for classes of finite undirected graphs, these conjectures remain open.”
